pages.text: An elderly turtle felt around the porch. "My glasses are gone." Kota hurried to help him find them.
Under a cushion, behind the table, beside the shoes—Kota searched everywhere, but found no glasses.
The turtle looked sad. "Everything is blurry." Kota's heart sank, too.
Dad said, "Searching everywhere can tangle us up. Let's follow his path backward." Kota got ready for a new game.
Before the porch, the turtle had been in the bath. Kota hopped backward toward it. "Hop back along the path!"
There were no glasses by the changing porch. Before his bath, the turtle had drunk tea on the yard platform.
Beside a cushion on the platform lay the folded glasses! Kota carried them carefully in both paws, tail held high.
The turtle put them on. "There you are! What a handsome face!" Kota's cheeks turned pink.
Kota hopped and looked back. "One, where was it last seen? Two, go backward! Three, found it!" The path held the answer.
Dad stroked Kota on his lap. "The path remembers things we've lost." Kota hopped backward all the way to bed.
